chapter_theme: Yoga as the third path: the yogi sits still as a post, unmoved by touch, and finds Siva blossoming within the soul like scent in a flower, the Lord whom Hari and Brahma sought for ages and who dwells in the crown. Learning and the arts do not end the bonds; the yogic way does, and the chapter ends with yoga's four grades.
structure_note: The yogi's stillness (1457), the Lord perceived only by those who perceive (1458 to 1460), the inner method over learning (1461), practice done with longing (1462), the inner fire (1463), the many who fell and the few who love (1464), an obscure verse on the paths within yoga (1465), and yoga's samaya, visesha, nirvana and abhisheka (1466), matching 1450 and 1476.

1457.reading: Going by the path and becoming one within rectitude, setting themselves like a planted post, for those who know the sign and do not start whether scratched or struck, union becomes possible.
1457.nuance: தறி இருந்தாற்போல் (like a post standing) is the image of the motionless seated yogi; not flinching at scratch or blow marks withdrawal from the senses. குறி (the sign, or the goal) is a recurring yogic term in Tirumular whose exact referent the verse leaves open.

1458.reading: He lets himself be perceived age after age only by those who perceive him; Hari who rests on the ocean and Brahma strove for ages, and he is in the crown.
1458.nuance: ஒருச்சி is read as உச்சி, the crown of the head, where yoga places the meeting with Siva; it may also be the summit beyond the gods' reach. The verse recalls the story of Hari and Brahma seeking his foot and crown (chapter 41).

1459.reading: As scent dwells in a flower, the fragrance of Siva has blossomed within the soul; for the knowers who perceive it steady as a painting, it is the central post joined with musk.
1459.nuance: The first two lines are plain: Siva in the soul as scent in the flower. ஓவியம் போல (like a painting) may describe the still yogi or the stable vision. நாவி அணைந்த நடுதறி (the planted middle post joined with musk) is taken by tradition as the central channel, sushumna; that is symbolic and uncertain. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Tiruppugazh 239 on the soul as Siva's form.

1460.reading: You say 'we are saved' but do not see the thing to be reached; if you see clearly in your mind Nandi who mingles in the fragrant flower, and darkness leaves, he is the root seed of your former births.
1460.nuance: The flower and scent carry on from 1459. The last line can mean the Lord was always the root seed of one's births, or that clear seeing destroys the seed of birth; the verse doesn't say which.

1461.reading: Letters, songs and the sixty-four arts do not remove birth bound in fetters with blame at its head; I have come to know the way of sending the moon, fire and sun up the path.
1461.nuance: The plain point is that learning (எழுத்து, பாடல், எண்ணெண் கலை) does not end the bonds. சோமன், அங்கி, அருக்கன் (moon, fire, sun) are traditionally the three channels or the three zones of the yogic body, and வழித்தலை செய்யும் (turning them up the path) a yogic method; that reading is tradition's.

1462.reading: If done standing in longing, one becomes a true ascetic; done in longing, it becomes true speech; done in longing, true tapas; done in longing, one becomes a dweller of heaven.
1462.nuance: The verse does not name what is done; under the heading it is yoga. மேய்த்தவர் is probably மெய்த்தவர் (true ascetics). The fourfold repetition of விரும்பி நின்றே செயின் puts the weight on desire held steadily, not on the practice.

1463.reading: If cherished, he grants the world of no birth; if seen, he stands within his own union; if without shame, he opens the way to the path of hell: the excellent one is the fire that burns in the flesh.
1463.nuance: ஊனில் சுடும் அங்கி (the fire that burns in the flesh) is traditionally the inner fire of yoga, and the verse calls it உத்தமன், the Lord. நாணில் may be 'if shamed' or 'without shame', and நகர நெறி may be the path to hell (நரகம்) or to the city (of Siva). So the third line either warns or promises; I have taken it as a warning, with the plain contrast of a fire that frees or harms.

1464.reading: Kings of just sceptre and endless great ascetics, countless thousands, have fallen; the siddhas, the gods and the three in their greatness come in love, saying 'this one is the Father'.
1464.nuance: The two halves are not joined by any word. They may contrast the many who fell, for all their rule and austerity, with those who reached him by love; or say that even siddhas and gods only love him. மூவர் (the three) is usually Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra.

1465.reading: For the yogi there are three, yoga and the rest, taken up; kiriyai and the rest belong to the body as chariyai; chariyai that has left thirst is one; within that one I placed my love in devotion to the Sun.
1465.nuance: The verse seems to subdivide yoga by the four paths (chariyai within yoga and so on), as 1474 does for jnana, but the lines are too compressed to fix. ஆதித்தன் (the Sun) may be the Lord as light, or the sun of the yogic body. Reading tentative throughout.

1466.reading: Yoga-samaya is contemplating the many yogas; yoga-visesha is eight-limbed yoga; yoga-nirvana is the rising of the Supreme that is reached; yoga-abhisheka is gaining bright siddhi.
1466.nuance: The four stages repeat the four initiations of 1450 (samaya, visesha, nirvana, abhisheka) as grades within yoga. பரோதயம் (the rising of the Supreme) is technical. The verse makes siddhi the crown of yoga, where 1476 makes the guru's feet the crown of jnana.

links.note: 375 tells how Hari and Brahma went to the crown and the foot and could not reach him; 1458 recalls their ages of striving and places him in the crown, perceived only by those who perceive.
The same four grades, samaya, visesha, nirvana and abhisheka, are initiations in 1450 and stages of yoga in 1466.

The Kural says those who learn and know the truth here do not come back; Tirumular says letters, songs and the sixty-four arts do not remove birth, and only the yogic way does. The difference may lie in what each means by learning.

source_issues: 1462: மேய்த்தவர் is probably a misreading of மெய்த்தவர்.
1465: the verse is very compressed and may be corrupt; the division of paths within yoga can't be recovered with confidence.
